newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chartists - Germany's DAX to hit 2,850 by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Chartists - Germany's DAX to hit 2,850 by year-end.

text.p: The DAX index of German shares is feeling vertigo at its current heights of 2,700 points and the overbought market will fall to 2,600 points before coming back to 2,850 points by Christmas, chartists said on Monday.
The DAX index has been on a record-breaking run for weeks, closing on an all-time high of 2,683.28 points and ending floor trade on Monday again at a record bourse high of 2,702.64.

"The position looks pretty rosy at the moment and I see no reason to think that it won't continue long term. We're looking at 2,850 points by the end of the year," Marcel Mussler, chartist at DG Bank in Frankfurt, told Reuters.

Technical analysts agree that the overall trend for the German share index is upwards. However, some kind of reversal is widely expected as the market is currently overbought after frenetic buying activity which has driven recent gains.

The market has advanced strongly, but more importantly, steadily, in the recent rally, chartists say. But the DAX is now feeling a touch of vertigo at these levels and needs to consolidate before continuing its rise to 2,850 by year-end.
While chartists generally agree that the overall trend in the coming weeks is upwards, they disagree about the level of consolidation to be expected in the short-term.
Mussler said: "The market is overheated at the moment and we will see some kind of consolidation but it shouldn't do too much damage."
Giro Olbertz, chartist at Vereins-und-WestBank in Hamburg, agrees.
"I'm cautious about the DAX in the short-term. After the recent rally the market is extremely overbought," said Olbertz.

"In the next three weeks or so, we are looking at a correction down to 2,600 points because the market is so overbought. After the correction the market should go up to around 2,800 points," said Olbertz.

"We're on a knife edge at the moment. For every record close we've had recently, you have to be ready for the market to go down three times as quick -- it could go down fifty ticks in a clip," said Paul Lewis, technical trader at BNP Bank in Frankfurt
Giro Olbertz bases his oversold argument on Relative Strength Indicators (RSI), which measures the strength of the day's price in relation to a previous period.
Nine-day RSI figures on the IBIS DAX are at their highest level for eight months, he says.

"In spite of the recent rally, it is encouraging to see there is little euphoria in the market. The moving averages (MAs) look good too. The 40-day MAs indicate good support at 2,600 points," said Olbertz.
Mussler says that the 38-day moving average is rising steeply, which indicates strength in the upward trend.
"The steeper the rise of the 38-day moving average, the less credible it becomes that the upward trend will suffer serious injury," said Mussler.
